clue.text: Handle husband with maturity

parts.note: a husband is a man, informally 'her man'
maturity is coming of age

explanation.surface: Advice on dealing with a husband: bring maturity to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a situation is to cope with or control it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: In wet soft earth, young dog finds salamander

parts.note: mud is wet soft earth
a puppy is a young dog

explanation.surface: A puppy finds a salamander in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: The mudpuppy is a North American aquatic salamander that keeps its external gills.

clue.text: Space agency, first to learn about the nose

parts.note: the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of learn

explanation.surface: The space agency is the first to find out something about noses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, so 'about the nose' describes it adjectivally.

clue.text: Having jar, we hear, with one from Perth, perhaps causes an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for jar is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: to grate is to jar, to irritate harshly
Perth here is the Scottish city, so someone from there is a Scot

explanation.surface: Over a drink with a man from Perth, something prompts a cry of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth suggests Australia, but the Scottish city gives the native; jar is a verb meaning grate, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Scott is an old-fashioned interjection expressing amazement.

clue.text: Inspector of buildings showing very sour disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the preceding letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A building inspector turns up in a thoroughly bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' reads as temperament, matching 'sour', but here it means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor examines property and reports on its structural condition for buyers or lenders.

clue.text: At college, harps go in it, surprisingly, and keyboard instruments

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected turn, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Harps unexpectedly make their way into a college music room alongside keyboards.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright pianos are keyboard instruments with vertical strings, the common domestic type.

clue.text: One using no animal products, say, is in the forefront

indicators.note: is in places the first item inside the second

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example, i.e. say

explanation.surface: Someone who avoids animal products is in the vanguard of a trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan is a person who eats and uses nothing derived from animals.

clue.text: Sensational marine creature mostly found in this stretch of water

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: yellow journalism is sensational reporting
a seal is a sea mammal

explanation.surface: A spectacular sea animal is mostly seen in these waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellow Sea lies between China and Korea, a named body of water.

clue.text: Fame bothered Peter Ustinov at first

indicators.note: bothered means stirred up, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the surname

parts.note: the first letter of Ustinov

explanation.surface: The actor Peter Ustinov was troubled by celebrity early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation or renown, a synonym of fame.

clue.text: Pharmacist giving drugs, initially, to one poet

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of drugs
the Roman numeral for one
Edmund Spenser, Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A chemist hands medicines over to a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser is one who makes up and issues medicines, a term for a pharmacist or chemist.

clue.text: Trip over mat in quiet church making a row

indicators.note: in means the joined words go inside the pair that follows
in a down clue over means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an outing is a trip
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a mat in a silent church and a fuss breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' reads as stumbling; it is a noun meaning an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A shouting match is a loud quarrel, which is what a row (rhyming with cow) means.

clue.text: Dance with girl at work

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Dancing with a girl from the office.
explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in quick two-four time.

clue.text: Dark line in one

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second, so one wraps around the other

parts.note: a unit is a single one
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Darkness in a single line, a terse riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere with no lights on is dark; the adjective swaps cleanly.

clue.text: Part of church grant fool squandered

indicators.note: money squandered is scattered about, so these letters are thrown into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foolish person wasted a grant meant for the church fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ loft is the raised gallery in a church where the organ stands.

clue.text: Napoleon, back in charge, halts state of emergency

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: Napoleon (nap) is a card game, short form nap
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
stations are halts, places where trains stop

explanation.surface: Napoleon returns to power and an emergency is declared.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is not the emperor but the card game, usually shortened to nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic stations is an idiom for a state of alarm in which everyone rushes to deal with a crisis.

clue.text: Neck and neck contest at Berlin, I suspect

indicators.note: I suspect hints at something doubtful or not as it seems, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator predicts a very close race at the Berlin games.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' does double duty in the surface but is plain fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail-biter is a contest so tense and close that onlookers chew their nails.

clue.text: OTT, like a company chairman?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: over the top, as in going too far
second meaning, split in two: a chairman is above the board of directors

explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British slang for over the top, excessive. The question mark flags the playful second reading, split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To go overboard is to behave excessively, and a chairman sits over the board in rank.

clue.text: Name horrible site for insects

parts.note: a term is a name for something

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone names a dreadful site full of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are wood-eating social insects that build large mounds.

clue.text: Concentrated on Prudence getting special medical treatment?

parts.note: intensive means concentrated on one area
prudence is care, caution

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence is the focus of attention as she receives treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence looks like a patient's name, but it is just the common noun meaning caution.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive care is the hospital department giving constant specialist treatment to the gravely ill.

clue.text: Reportedly films composer

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: films are coats, thin layers

explanation.surface: Reports say the films are by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' is not cinema but thin coverings.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Coates was an English composer of light music, including the Dambusters March.

clue.text: Male shoots, in sultanate, one appointed to investigate complaints

indicators.note: in means one group of letters sits inside another

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
M is the abbreviation for male
buds are young shoots on a plant

explanation.surface: A man fires shots somewhere in a Gulf sultanate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' reads as a verb of firing; it is the noun for new plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official who looks into public grievances against organisations.

clue.text: Husband in food shop in capital

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word for the shop

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband shops at a delicatessen in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, in the form of New Delhi, is the capital of India.

clue.text: Broom kept in wardrobe, sometimes

indicators.note: kept in says the letters are stored inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A broom is sometimes stored in the wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom made of twigs tied around a stick, the witch's broomstick kind.

clue.text: US writer set off home

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: An American author sets off for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was an American writer and modernist patron living in Paris.

clue.text: Come to very young child the Parisienne rejected

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the French article is read backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman turns away a little child who comes to her.
explanation.definitionFit: To total a sum is to amount to it, as a bill comes to a figure.

clue.text: Will short examination involving volunteers (soldiers)?

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one part wraps round the rest

parts.note: a test is a brief exam
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: Will a quick test be set for volunteer soldiers?
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, as in the legal phrase last will and testament.

clue.text: Respectable poker hand

definitions.meaning: second meaning: five cards in sequence

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a decent poker hand; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an upright, conventional person and also a run of five consecutive cards in poker.

clue.text: University teacher is after a handsome young man

parts.note: taken as written
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecturer chasing a good-looking young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the teacher-and-is part follows the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name stands for any good-looking young man.
